issue_context.title: Some azure _info modules still return ansible_facts when called as _info
issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY
Some of the modules still return something in `ansible_facts`, even though the result in there is an empty list:
 - ~~`azure_rm_publicipaddress_info`~~
 - ~~`azure_rm_networkinterface_info`~~
 - `azure_rm_storageaccount_info`
 - `azure_rm_virtualmachineimage_info`
 - `azure_rm_virtualmachinescaleset_info`
 - `azure_rm_virtualnetwork_info`

Finally, `azure_rm_resourcegroup_info` always returns `ansible_facts` with content (which is also returned as non-`ansible_facts`).

When called as `_info` modules, these modules should not have anything in `ansible_facts` when returning.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
~~azure_rm_publicipaddress_info~~
~~azure_rm_networkinterface_info~~
azure_rm_resourcegroup_info
azure_rm_storageaccount_info
azure_rm_virtualmachineimage_info
azure_rm_virtualmachinescaleset_info
azure_rm_virtualnetwork_info

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
```paste below
2.9
```

review_comments: Ditto, the facts module never returned non facts
Should only be returned on _info calls.

This one did not return `storageaccounts` in `stable-2.8`: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/stable-2.8/lib/ansible/modules/cloud/azure/azure_rm_storageaccount_facts.py#L335

The Azure team apparently did decide to change that for 2.9.
Shouldn't this go before the part above this where you are setting `self.results`. I'm struggling to see how this even affects the results in the facts module case.

I didn't want to reorganize the code :) but yes, it makes more sense. `result` is a list, so even after assinging it to `self.results`, modifying it will affect the output.

I'll change the order.
Shouldn't this only be returned for the non facts module?

~~`dnsrecordsets` is the regular return value of the module; `ansible_facts.azure_dnsrecordset` is only returned when the module is called as `_facts` (i.e. when `is_old_facts` is `True`).~~ Sorry, got confused.

It already returned that in `stable-2.8`: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/stable-2.8/lib/ansible/modules/cloud/azure/azure_rm_dnsrecordset_facts.py#L212

(There were quite a lot of `_facts` modules which returned information also as non-facts, sometimes even just as non-facts. This apparently belongs to the former category.)
Fair enough, I suppose this probably applies to most of my other comments below.
It did, but not to all :)
